battle.name: 楊堅平王謙之戰
battle.brief: 北周大象二年（580）冬，并州總管王謙乘楊堅專政、諸將蠢動之際起兵於太原，關中宿衛與關東州兵奉詔討之，韋師、韋冲、韋世康分道出師；開皇二年（582）春，叛軍五萬眾在并州地界被擊破，斬首萬餘級、俘其將趙乞兒，餘眾四散，王謙困守太原而終。此役掃清北周宿將最後一股成建制武裝，楊堅自此得以專力南下滅陳。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一方是北周朝廷與剛剛接掌朝政的楊堅，一方是并州總管王謙舉起來的叛軍。北周方面的軍政骨幹在長安：大象元年至二年，楊堅先後為大丞相、錄尚書事，進封相國、隋王，加九錫與殊禮，劍履上殿、冕十二旒，總百揆而監軍國；軍隊以府兵為骨幹，關中、關東、涼州、隴右的鄉兵常備於籍，京師宿衛的殿中士、羽林、虎賁拱衛禁中，此外還有各州鎮守的軍與諸軍府統率的部曲，隨時可以調動。叛軍方面靠的是王謙在并州的實權：并州治太原，據汾水之旁，北倚雁門、井陘之險，東當滹沱、井陘之口，是關中軍資北上的門戶，也是北周邊軍馬匹、芻粟與弓箭手的主要來源之一；王氏世代與宇文氏通姻，其父王雄位至上柱國、大將軍，曾在周明帝初年率軍入蜀、攻下成都，滅掉陳朝在益州的統治，王謙承襲了這份在關東的軍望。周宣帝即位後他以開府儀同三司出為并州總管，掌晉北的軍政人事。周室傾覆在即，關隴集團與河北、山西一帶世族、宿將之間的權力拉扯，才是這場叛亂真正的土壤。陳朝在江南本可乘虛策應，但其開皇元年正月攻金鄉之役失利，北方邊防空虛而主力受損，只能有限度地回應；北邊的突厥同時在牽制隋廷的注意力，楊堅因此不能容忍并州久拖不決。
countriesEn: The two parties in this war were on one side the court of Northern Zhou together with Yang Jian, who had just taken charge of the government, and on the other the rebel army raised by Wang Qian, the commander of Bingzhou. The military and political core of the Zhou court lay at Chang'an: between the first and second years of the Daxiang era Yang Jian successively served as Grand Chancellor and as recorder of the department of state affairs, was advanced to the rank of Xiangguo and Prince of Sui, was granted the nine bestowments and exceptional honours, was permitted to wear his sword and enter in court boots, and wore a crown of twelve pendants; he took charge of all affairs of state and of the army. The troops rested on the fubing militia system, with the households of Guanzhong, Guandong, Liangzhou and Longyou enrolled for standing service, the palace guards drawn from the dianzhong shi, yulin and hu ben who garrisoned the capital, and in addition the garrisons of the various prefectures and the private retainers commanded by the military bureaus, all of which could be moved at need. The rebel side relied on the actual authority Wang Qian held in Bingzhou: the prefecture was administered from Taiyuan, beside the Fen River, protected on the north by the passes of Yanmen and Jingxing and facing on the east the outlets of the Hutuo and the road through Jingxing, so Bingzhou was the doorway through which the war stores of Guanzhong moved north, and one of the principal sources of horses, fodder and archers for the Zhou frontier army. The Wang clan had intermarried with the Yuwen house for generations; Wang Qian's father Wang Xiong had risen to the rank of Upper Pillar of State and General, and in the first years of Emperor Ming of Zhou had led an army into Shu and taken Chengdu, ending the Chen dynasty's rule in Yizhou, and Wang Qian inherited that military standing in the eastern provinces. After Emperor Xuan of Zhou took the throne he left the capital as commander of Bingzhou and took charge of troops, appointments and supplies in northern Shanxi. The Zhou house was about to fall, and the real soil of this rebellion was the tug of war for authority between the Guanzhong military group and the aristocratic and old-command families of Hebei and Shanxi. The Chen dynasty across the Yangtze might have exploited the opening, but it had suffered a reverse at Jinxiang in the first month of the Kaihuang era, so its northern front was hollow and its main force damaged, and it could only respond in a limited way; the Turks on the northern frontier were at the same time tying down the court's attention, so Yang Jian could not tolerate Bingzhou remaining unresolved for long.
people: 決定這場戰爭走向的是楊堅與王謙兩人，加上被捲入其中的北周舊將與并州官屬。楊堅在北周末年以大丞相、相國的身份總攬軍國，進爵加錫已名實兼備；他先用一年時間平掉相州趙王宇文招、越王宇文盛藉詔書發動的變亂，又在同年冬天擊破鄴城的尉遲迥，把北周宗室與河北世族最能打的三股力量一一拆散，隨後才有餘裕回頭對付并州。并州總管王謙是太原祁人，父王雄為北周名將，入蜀擒成都之役的主攻者；王謙少有武藝，趫捷過人，周武帝時已為開府儀同三司，宣帝即位後出鎮并州，握晉北的兵馬錢糧。他起兵並不是出於北周舊制的理由，而是出於不願看楊堅把軍權收歸中央；隋末並州一門父子相繼，楊堅對王氏的疑忌也由此而生。隋方派出的三員主將都是關中舊族：杜陵韋氏的韋師、韋冲、韋世康，韋師與韋冲皆位上柱國，韋世康時任尚書右僕射，是朝中老臣；三人分道出師，把王謙在野外的戰力先行壓住。叛軍主將趙乞兒率五萬眾出戰被擒，首級數與俘獲成為此役最硬的一筆記錄。陳朝一端，開皇初北伐的將領郝叔文、馬幼昌等曾在金鄉大破隋軍，其時正想利用并州的變亂反過來牽制北方，終未能成行。周靜帝宇文闌、趙王宇文招、尉遲迥這些北周舊人，也在半年之內相繼成為楊堅要清掉的對象，而王謙是最後一個。
peopleEn: The men who decided the course of this war were Yang Jian and Wang Qian, together with the old Zhou generals and the Bingzhou officials who were caught up in it. In the last years of Northern Zhou Yang Jian, as Grand Chancellor and Xiangguo, held all power in state and army, and his elevation and the bestowments he had received were both name and substance. First he spent a year putting down the revolt in Xiangzhou raised by the Prince of Zhao Yuwen Zhao and the Prince of Yue Yuwen Sheng on the strength of a forged edict, and then in the winter of the same year he broke Wei Chi Jiong at Ye, breaking up one after another the three strongest armed groups of the Zhou princes and the Hebei aristocracy; only afterwards did he have the margin to turn back on Bingzhou. Wang Qian, commander of Bingzhou, was a native of Qixian in Taiyuan. His father Wang Xiong was one of the famous Zhou generals, the leading attacker in the campaign that took Chengdu in Shu. Wang Qian himself was quick and strong, and had already been made a Gentleman of the Three Excellencies under Emperor Wu of Zhou; after Emperor Xuan took the throne he was posted to Bingzhou and held the troops, horses, money and grain of northern Shanxi. He did not rise in revolt for any reason drawn from the old institutions of Zhou, but simply because he would not watch Yang Jian gather the command of the army into the central government; the father and son of the Wang house held Bingzhou in succession, and Yang Jian's suspicion of the family grew accordingly. The three commanders the Sui sent out were all of the old clans of Guanzhong: Wei Shi, Wei Chong and Wei Shikang of the Du-ling Wei house, Wei Shi and Wei Chong both being Upper Pillars of State, while Wei Shikang was then Right Vice-Director of the Department of State Affairs, an old minister of the court. They advanced by separate routes and crushed Wang Qian's field strength first. The rebel commander Zhao Qier marched out with fifty thousand men and was taken prisoner, and the count of heads and the capture form the hardest single record of the battle. On the Chen side, generals such as Hao Shaowen and Ma Youchang had beaten a Sui army at Jinxiang early in the Kaihuang era, and they would have used the disturbance in Bingzhou to pull at the north instead, but the attempt never came off. Zhou Jingdi Yuwen Lan, the Prince of Zhao Yuwen Zhao, and Wei Chi Jiong all became targets Yang Jian had to remove within half a year, and Wang Qian was the last of them.
kits: 卡面上這件亞述長弓並不出現在并州，但它所代表的那一類技術在五八〇年的中國正是軍隊的骨幹：反曲的複合弓，弓背以角、筋、木層層複合，短而有力，拉滿之後能保持張力，這是亞述人用弓與鐵的組合橫掃兩河流域的資本。放到北周的軍制裡，同樣功能的武器是弓與弩：蹶張弩以足力張弦，擘張弩以腰臂之力張弦，良弓配羽箭供騎兵與步卒施射，弩則是攻城與野戰的骨幹火力，北方軍隊格外看重弩手，野戰與攻城都以弩陣為前驅，再以精騎踏平殘陣。騎兵用角弓與鳴鏃，步卒以大盾與長槍護住弩手；甲胄以鐵葉為主，良工鍛造的明光鐵甲供侍衛與騎將使用，軍中另以皮甲、青銅鍔與大量札甲維持裝備量。馬匹來自河西、涼州與并州邊軍，輜重車與牛車運載糧秣、箭矢與攻城器械，巢車、撞車、雲梯、飛石車在圍城時推到城下；糧道沿汾水與井陘、蒲津的水陸轉運維持。亞述弓兵在車上發矢、車兵靠弓兵開路的那套配合，在五八〇年的北方已經換成騎射與弩兵開路、步卒隨進的樣子：戰車自兩晉以後基本退出軍陣，車上的弓手改由騎兵與步兵分擔，而先用弓弩壓住對方陣腳、再以鐵騎與重步兵踏平殘陣的道理，正落在王謙與韋師、韋冲交手的這片汾河谷地裡。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card never appeared at Bingzhou, but the class of technology it represents was the backbone of the Chinese army in 580: the recurved composite bow, its belly built up in layers of horn, sinew and wood, short and powerful, able to hold its tension once drawn at full, and that was the capital with which the Assyrians swept the Two Rivers with the combination of bow and iron. Translated into the military institutions of Northern Zhou, the weapons serving the same function were the bow and the crossbow: the foot-drawn crossbow (jue zhang nu) was strung with the legs, the shoulder-drawn crossbow (bo zhang nu) with the waist and arms, good bows with feathered arrows served the cavalry and the foot, and the crossbow was the backbone firepower of both field and siege, the northern armies placing particular value on crossbowmen, who formed the van in the field and at the walls, after which compact cavalry rode down the broken enemy. The cavalry used horn bows and whistling arrows; the foot protected the crossbowmen with large shields and long spears. Armour was built mainly of iron plates, the fine forged ming-guang iron harness being for guards and mounted commanders, while the troops maintained their numbers with leather armour, bronze throat-guards and a great many lacquered lamellar plates. Horses came from Hexi, Liangzhou and the Bingzhou frontier garrisons, and covered wagons and ox-carts carried grain, fodder, arrows and siege engines; the mobile tower, the battering ram, the scaling ladder and the stone-thrower were pushed up to the walls during a siege. The supply line was kept alive by water and land transport along the Fen River and through the Jingxing and Pujin crossings. The Assyrian combination of archers shooting from the chariot, with the chariotry following the archers' lead, had by 580 in the north taken a different shape: the war chariot had largely left the order of battle after the two Jin, the archers on the platform were replaced by cavalry and foot, and the principle of using the bow and the crossbow to crush the enemy's line before committing the iron cavalry and the heavy infantry was precisely the principle applied on the Fen River plain where Wang Qian met Wei Shi and Wei Chong.
tactics: 叛軍與官軍的戰法都帶有晉北地形的特徵。王謙據太原，倚汾水天險與城郭之固，卻不願坐困，於是把主力推出城外：趙乞兒率五萬眾迎戰隋師於并州地界，試圖以人數與地勢彌補器械與訓練之差，一戰而敗，退保城池，分兵固守諸郡，又遣使向陳朝求援，冀望南北同時發動以牽制隋軍。官軍這邊不用硬攻：三路大軍自關中、洛陽一線分道北上，沿汾河谷地與井陘、蒲津諸道抵達太原，先以弓弩壓制城外與城頭，剪除騎兵與遊騎的活動空間，再合兵攻其鋒，務求在野戰中吃掉叛軍的機動兵力，而不把主力耗在城下的攻堅上。韋師、韋冲、韋世康分兵合圍的同時派人招撫叛軍的將校，切斷叛軍對外求援與糧秣接濟的通道，籍此分化太原以外的郡縣；同時安撫北周的舊將與河北世族，穩住關東，避免戰線拉長。戰事自大象二年冬起兵，至開皇二年（582）春主力潰散，前後跨年而未大決，說明雙方都在等對方先動：以楊堅的位置，多拖一日就多一分被北方突厥與陳朝聯手利用的風險，所以官軍一旦集結到位便不給叛軍喘息之機。
tacticsEn: The methods of both sides carried the marks of the terrain of northern Shanxi. Wang Qian held Taiyuan, leaning on the natural defence of the Fen River and on the walls of the city, yet unwilling to sit still; so he pushed his main force out into the open: Zhao Qier met the Sui army with fifty thousand men in the territory of Bingzhou, trying to make up for the difference in equipment and training with numbers and favourable ground, was defeated in a single engagement, fell back into the city, split his troops to hold the various commanderies, and sent envoys to the Chen court for help, hoping that north and south would move at the same time to pin the Sui army. On the government side there was no assault on the walls: three columns marched north by separate routes from the Guanzhong and Luoyang line, reached Taiyuan along the valley of the Fen River and by the roads through Jingxing and Pujin, first used bows and crossbows to dominate the field outside the walls and the walls themselves and to cut off the room in which the rebel cavalry and raiders could move, and only then closed to strike the enemy's spearhead, aiming to destroy the rebels' mobile strength in open battle rather than to spend the main force on a direct siege of the city. While Wei Shi, Wei Chong and Wei Shikang converged from their separate columns, emissaries went out to win over the rebel officers, cutting the rebel side off from foreign aid and from supplies and thereby dividing the commanderies outside Taiyuan; at the same time they pacified the old generals of Zhou and the Hebei aristocracy, to hold the east firm and prevent the front from stretching. The war began with the rising at Taiyuan in the winter of the second year of Daxiang and ended with the main rebel force breaking up in the spring of the second year of Kaihuang (582), spanning a year without a decisive battle, which shows that both sides were waiting for the other to move first. In Yang Jian's position, every extra day of delay meant extra risk of the Turks in the north and the Chen court in the south exploiting the situation together; so once the government columns were concentrated and in position, no breathing space was left to the rebels.
data: 可核的數字不多，但仍有幾處可以據以描繪這場戰爭的規模。《資治通鑑》記叛軍出兵之數為五萬，隋軍以韋師、韋冲、韋世康三人為主將，分道出師，集中關中宿衛與關東諸州之兵遠出，並非小股偏師。野戰一役，隋軍斬首萬餘級，並生擒叛軍主將趙乞兒，這是全戰場最硬的一個數字，也說明叛軍的精銳在第一次決戰裡便折損過半。地理與時間上，長安至太原的道路約近千里，隋軍沿汾河谷地北上，糧秣須由關中經河東轉運，太原一線的存糧與芻草供應，直接決定圍城與野戰能撐多久；天氣上，太原盆地冬春苦寒，汾河結冰可行軍，卻使糧船難以暢行，雙方都受制於同一段水運。時間上，叛軍自大象二年（580）冬舉兵，主要戰事落在開皇元年（581）至開皇二年（582），開皇二年春天的會戰結束了大部分戰事，其後零星抵抗延續數月，王謙本人死於敗亡，至開皇二、三年間部眾盡散。同一時期，陳朝曾撥出北援的兵將，但記錄殘缺，兵數與戰果各家說法不一；北邊的突厥也在同時段南窺，隋廷必須速戰速決。
dataEn: There are few numbers that can be checked, but a few can still be used to sketch the scale of this war. The Zizhi Tongjian records the rebel force as fifty thousand men when it marched out. On the Sui side the commanders were Wei Shi, Wei Chong and Wei Shikang, who advanced by separate routes with troops drawn from the palace guards of Guanzhong and the various prefectures of Guandong sent far afield; this was not a small detachment. In the field engagement the Sui army cut off more than ten thousand heads and took the rebel commander Zhao Qier alive, the hardest single figure of the whole battle, and one that shows the rebel elite losing more than half its strength in the first decisive encounter. In geography and in time, the road from Chang'an to Taiyuan runs nearly a thousand li, and the Sui army moved north along the valley of the Fen River, with grain and fodder carried by the transport of Guanzhong through Hedong. The stores of grain and fodder along the Taiyuan line decided directly how long the siege and the field battle could last. As for the weather, the Taiyuan basin is bitter cold in winter and spring; the Fen freezes hard enough to carry an army on the ice, yet the grain boats cannot run freely, and both sides were constrained by the same stretch of water transport. In time, the rebels rose in the winter of the second year of Daxiang (580), and the main fighting fell in the first and second years of Kaihuang (581-582); the engagement in the spring of the second year of Kaihuang ended the greater part of the war, scattered resistance dragging on for some months, and Wang Qian himself died of his reverse, his followers dispersing by the second and third years of Kaihuang. At the same time the Chen court did send troops and officers to the north in support, but the record is fragmentary and the numbers and results differ from account to account; the Turks on the northern frontier were also probing southward in the same period, and the Sui court could not afford a long war.
cause: 王謙起兵的緣由有三層。最外一層是北周末年的體制失衡：宇文氏自庾信、宇文護一路傳下來的宗室領兵、宿將鎮州的老例，到隋國公楊堅手上已經行不通；楊堅以大丞相代周，四處安插自己人，把兵馬錢糧的調度權收歸中樞，并州這樣的大鎮因此感到威脅。第二層是家族與私人的利害：王雄父子在北周關東握有并州的實際控制，王謙不肯交出，也沒有把這份控制轉化為朝堂位置的通道——他既不是宇文氏宗室，也沒能進入楊堅新組的班底，於是只能選擇自保。第三層是時機：大象二年，楊堅加九錫、進相國、廢周靜帝、準備受禪的動作接連完成，同一年裡相州有趙王宇文招、鄴城有尉遲迥各自舉兵，北方看來仍是群雄並立；王謙判斷楊堅會被這兩處拖住，於是趁亂在并州舉兵，遣使向陳朝求援，想造出一個南北夾擊的局面。楊堅的反應同樣清楚：尉遲迥與趙王的亂事必須先平，否則并州與河北、關東會連成一氣；等鄴城平定，他便把兵鋒轉向太原，因為并州一旦久拖，陳朝便有了可乘之機，北方突厥也會趁虛南下。
causeEn: There were three layers to the reasons Wang Qian rose in revolt. The outermost was the imbalance of the institutions of late Northern Zhou: the old practice of the Yuwen house, handed down through Yuwen Xin and Yuwen Hu, of princes commanding armies and old generals holding prefectures, no longer worked under Yang Jian, Prince of Sui. Taking the place of the Zhou court as Grand Chancellor, Yang Jian placed his own men everywhere and gathered the right to move troops, money and grain into the central government, and great prefectures such as Bingzhou felt the threat. The second layer was the interest of the family: Wang Xiong and his son held real control of Bingzhou in the eastern provinces of Zhou, and Wang Qian would not hand it over, nor had he found a channel to convert that control into a place in the new court at court. He was not of the Yuwen blood, and he had not been taken into the group Yang Jian was assembling, so all that remained was to protect himself. The third layer was timing: in the second year of Daxiang Yang Jian's bestowments, his elevation to Xiangguo, the deposition of Zhou Jingdi and the preparations for the transfer of the throne all followed one another in quick succession, and in that same year the Prince of Zhao Yuwen Zhao rose at Xiangzhou and Wei Chi Jiong rose at Ye, so the north still looked like a field of competing powers. Judging that Yang Jian would be held up by those two, Wang Qian rose at Bingzhou while the confusion lasted and sent envoys to the Chen court for help, hoping to create a situation in which north and south would strike together. Yang Jian's response was equally clear: the revolts of Wei Chi Jiong and the Prince of Zhao had to be settled first, or else Bingzhou would be joined to Hebei and Guandong in one line; and once Ye was taken, he turned the edge of his army towards Taiyuan, because if Bingzhou dragged on, the Chen court would have its opening and the Turks on the north would press in behind it.
impact: 平定王謙，對楊堅而言，等於把北周最後一個成建制的軍事集團從自己身邊拔掉。尉遲迥在鄴、王謙在并州，先後兩場兵變都是北周晚期將門自據一方這個老例的最後兩次實踐；兩場都平之後，北周的兵權不再分散在宗室與世族手裡，隋朝得以在關中宿衛之外重新編排北方的州鎮與總管府，把并州這樣的邊州變成對突厥的前線，而不是內部的隱患。對并州與山西的世族而言，王氏的覆亡意味著門第與軍功的傳統被中樞收編，地方的部曲、私兵與舊日障礙被逐步拆解，此後隋朝在北方的調度才真正順暢。戰略上，陳朝失去了在北方唯一成形的策應點：開皇初年它還能靠金鄉之役得手，如今連一個內應都指望不上，江北的防線只剩空架子，這也讓開皇九年（589）的滅陳之役再無北顧之虞。對楊堅個人而言，這場平亂的意義不在收穫，而在排除亂源：北方的秩序從此建立在開皇朝的中央調度之上，而他要對付的只剩下南方的陳朝和塞外的突厥。
impactEn: In putting down Wang Qian, Yang Jian removed from his own side the last organised military group of Northern Zhou. Wei Chi Jiong at Ye and Wang Qian at Bingzhou were the last two practical instances of the late Zhou practice by which a commander's house held a region on its own account. With both settled, the military authority of Zhou was no longer dispersed among princes and aristocratic houses, and the Sui could reorganise the prefectures and the offices of the commanders in the north around the guards of Guanzhong, turning a frontier prefecture such as Bingzhou into a platform against the Turks rather than a hidden trouble within the state. For the aristocratic families of Bingzhou and Shanxi, the fall of the Wang house meant that the tradition of lineage and military merit was taken over by the central government, that local retainers, private soldiers and the old obstacles were gradually broken up, and only then did the Sui's movements in the north run truly smooth. Strategically, the Chen court lost the only formed point of support it had in the north: early in the Kaihuang era it could still score at Jinxiang, but now it could not even count on a single agent, and the line north of the Yangtze was an empty shell, which left the campaign of 589 no cause for anxiety to the north. For Yang Jian personally the meaning of this pacification lay not in the spoil but in the removal of the source of disorder: the order of the north henceforth rested on the central dispatch of the Kaihuang court, and only the Chen court in the south and the Turks beyond the frontier remained for him to face.
result: 結果是官軍完勝。開皇二年（582）春天的會戰中，韋師、韋冲、韋世康各道兵馬擊破趙乞兒的五萬眾，斬首萬餘級，趙乞兒被俘；太原以外的郡縣見勢歸順，叛軍四散，王謙退保城中，既無援軍亦無糧秣，最終在困守中病死，所部隨之潰散，陳朝寄望的南北夾擊沒有成形。這場勝利帶來三樣東西：并州及晉北歸入隋朝的直接控制，楊堅得以在開皇年間放心地經營河北、江南與西域的商路與漕運，也讓隋朝在北方的軍制改以府兵與宿衛為主、地方宿將的私兵逐步裁汰。北周最後的宿將反亂至此全部結束，北方統一只餘南朝一線的陳朝。回頭看卡面那件亞述長弓：並州城下自然沒有亞述人的反曲複合弓與車載弓兵，當時真正架在城頭與陣前的，是蹶張弩、擘張弩與良弓羽箭；但亞述弓兵開路、車兵隨進的那套原理，在五八〇年的北方並未消失，只是載具由戰車換成騎兵與輜重車，火力由單兵弓換成弩陣——同樣是先以弓弩吃掉對方的陣腳與體力，再把主力壓上去。
resultEn: The result was a complete victory for the government forces. In the engagement of the spring of the second year of Kaihuang (582), the columns of Wei Shi, Wei Chong and Wei Shikang broke Zhao Qier's fifty thousand men, cut off more than ten thousand heads and took Zhao Qier prisoner. The commanderies outside Taiyuan came over as the tide turned, the rebels scattered, and Wang Qian fell back inside the city with neither aid nor supplies; he died in the siege and his followers broke up with him, and the pincer movement from north and south that the Chen court had hoped for never took shape. The victory brought three things with it: Bingzhou and northern Shanxi came under the direct control of the Sui; Yang Jian was able to work the trade routes and the grain transport of Hebei, Jiangnan and the western regions without anxiety during the Kaihuang years; and the military system of the north was reorganised with the fubing and the palace guards as its backbone while the private troops of local commanders were gradually reduced. The last rising of the old commanders of Northern Zhou was now completely over, and of the north only the Chen court in the south remained unconquered. Returning to the Assyrian bow on the card: there was of course no recurved composite bow and no chariot-borne archer below the walls of Taiyuan, and what actually stood on the ramparts and in front of the line were the foot-drawn and shoulder-drawn crossbows and good bows with feathered arrows. Yet the principle of the Assyrian archers opening the way for the chariotry had not vanished in the north of 580; only the vehicle had changed from the war chariot to the horseman and the covered wagon, and the firepower from the single bow to the crossbow line, and it was the same principle in both cases: first the bows and crossbows eat away at the enemy's line and its stamina, and then the main force is pressed forward on top of it.
